title: On Giving the last loaf to the children
subtitle: 互助关爱 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 互助关爱（社会服务与人际沟通·互助与关爱）
meta: 主题语境：互助关爱（社会服务与人际沟通·互助与关爱）　|　核心词汇：give　|　正文 350 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 give 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1959 the builder ① gave the last loaf to the children in public, and every assistant in the site said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three months on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the builder ② gives the last loaf to the children in silence without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ give the last loaf to the children at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ given the last loaf to the children before — a line in the plan for October 1953 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Giving the last loaf to the children in public, the builder said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the beam at the far wall, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ give a supper for thirty guests in silence, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Give a supper for thirty guests at once and never mention it again.

By 1966 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the plan, and a new assistant from the next site ⑧ gives a supper for thirty guests in public every month without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the wall, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ gave the last loaf to the children again when nobody else would.

⑩ To give the last loaf to the children, my mother said in 1971, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the site remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the site forgets, somebody gives the last loaf to the children in silence again and somebody must give the last loaf to the children in public all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 给（一般过去式 gave the last loaf to the children：1959 年施工员头一回这样做，当着众人面）
B. v. 给（一般现在 gives the last loaf to the children：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 给（不定式 to give the last loaf to the children：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 给（过去完成时 had given the last loaf to the children：1953 年十月的施工图上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 给（动名词 giving the last loaf to the children 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 举办（give a supper for thirty guests：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去举办为三十位客人办一顿晚饭）
G. v. 举办（give a supper for thirty guests：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 给（后段两处：新来的帮工照例 gives a supper for thirty guests，而母亲又一次 gave the last loaf to the children）

answers.why: give 意为“给”，1959 年施工员当着众人面给把最后那条面包给了孩子们，那是工地里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 gave。
give 意为“给”，自那以后施工员一言不发地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 gives。
give 意为“给”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯给把最后那条面包给了孩子们”，此处为不定式 to give the last loaf to the children。
give 意为“给”，施工图里 十月 那行字说明早在 1966 年之前就有人给过，故用过去完成时 had given。
give 意为“给”，施工员说“给把最后那条面包给了孩子们这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 giving the last loaf to the children 作主语。
give 意为“举办”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去举办为三十位客人办一顿晚饭”，should ever 之后用原形 give a supper for thirty guests。
give 意为“举办”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻举办为三十位客人办一顿晚饭（give a supper for thirty guests at once），以后再也不要提起。
give 意为“给”，新来的帮工每个月份都照例举办为三十位客人办一顿晚饭，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 gives。
give 意为“给”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次当着众人面给把最后那条面包给了孩子们，用一般过去式 gave 叙述。
give 意为“给”，结尾那句是母亲 1971 年的话：要给把最后那条面包给了孩子们，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和工地记住的那一件。

Three months on, the builder still gives the last loaf to the children in silence without being asked.
My mother said later that to give the last loaf to the children at all was the part nobody had expected.
Somebody had given the last loaf to the children long before 1966, and the line in the plan for October proves it.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 give 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1959 the builder gave the last loaf to the children in public, and nobody in the site forgot it.
Even now the builder gives the last loaf to the children in silence whenever the site asks.
Giving the last loaf to the children in public, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever give a supper for thirty guests in silence, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new assistant from the next site gives a supper for thirty guests in public every month, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother gave the last loaf to the children again, and the site remembered that half.
